Declare the column header, and the numbers it prints

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_col_header.Rd

plan_col_header() gives the column header, built with the same rtf_col_header() as everywhere else (or a row at a time with lines), and says what its {tokens} print: {col} the column, {n} the column's population, read from the ARD or given. A row shorter than the table has its last cell repeated over the value columns, whose names are not known until the table exists, so one header serves a study with two arms or five. It is a display verb: it runs on the pages, as set_col_header().

Usage

plan_col_header(
  .plan,
  header = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  header_sep = NULL,
  col_header_align = NULL,
  lines = NULL,
  span = "each"
)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

header

The header, one of:

an rtf_col_header()

the ordinary case. Its cells may carry {col} (the column; with several cols keys the leaf, and {col1}, {col2}, ... the levels in order) and {n}. A row already the right length, and a cell with no token, are untouched.

a data frame of cells

one row a cell, with the col_header sheet's columns (line, cols, span, text, borders ...), placed on each page's columns when it is made; how tflspec::tfl_table_code() writes a workbook's header.

a function

of the resolved n (and, with two arguments, the finished table), when the header has to be computed.

The tokens a cell may use besides {col} and {n}: {n:sum}, the number totalled over the columns the cell covers (a spanner over one arm shows that arm's N, one over all of them the study total), and {n:<column>}, the number of one named column ("A={n:Placebo}"). {n1}, {n2}, ... name a depth of the keys. print() of the plan lists every token it offers, with its values; see also plan_header_tokens().

values

What the {tokens} take. A named list, each name a token; one value that is not a list is taken as n:

list(n = TRUE)

(or TRUE) the population of each column, read from the ARD at every depth of the cols keys. Only a number the ARD states as a population size is read, the first of: a total stated by group (..ard_total_n.. keyed by the column, cards::ard_strata(.by = TRT01A, .f = ~ cards::ard_total_n(.x))); a cards sentinel's N (ard_stack_hierarchical(over_variables = TRUE), the stack's denominator); the column variable's own tabulation (the .key_own rows normalize_ard() keeps from ard_stack(.by = )); an analysis N that is a denominator by construction or that two variables agree on. So a header N that differs from the percentages' denominator is a total by group. What cannot be read prints NA, with one warning that says why.

list(n = "page"), list(n = "table")

for pages split by a group value (plan_paginate_group()): each page's own population (the ARD rows carrying the page key), or the analysis set's (the rows without it). list(n = "page", N = "table") gives both, as {n} and {N}. n = TRUE reads the page's, then the table's, and warns when both are stated and differ.

numbers

given by hand: a vector named by column key at any depth, n = c(Placebo = 20, Active = 20), or one unnamed number for every cell. After a workbook (tflspec::tfl_table_plan()) a later plan_col_header(values = ) supplies the numbers and keeps the workbook's header.

a function

of the data, returning one of the above, for a number neither can find.

more names

further tokens: list(n = TRUE, total = 254) makes {total} print 254 in a spanner over each column's {n}.

A data frame of per-page values is set_col_header()'s own values: one row per page key, a column per {token}. The study total is never put in every column: it answers a one-column table and a cell over all the columns. Keep the header consistent with the body: the percentages are over the denominator cards used.

A later plan_col_header(values = ) replaces the earlier values as a whole: a token or column the later call leaves out is not kept.

header_sep

as_rtftables()'s header_sep: the separator a plain table's column names are split on into spanning header rows.

col_header_align

rtftable()'s col_header_align.

lines

The header a row at a time, instead of header: a list, one element a header row (the top first), each a named character vector. A cell's name is the columns it sits on (a column name, .values for every value column, a position or range such as 3:5, or KEY = value), its value the text, with the same tokens: list(c(label = "", .values = "{col}"), c(label = "Characteristic", .values = "(N={n})")).

span

With lines: how a cell over several columns is made, one value for every cell or a list as lines is (each element the spans of that row's cells, named as its cells are):

"each"

(default) a cell a column.

"one"

one cell over them all: a spanner.

a key's name

a cell per value of that key.

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb; rtf_col_header(), plan_header_tokens(), plan_n_candidates().

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

st <- data.frame(
  ARM       = rep(c("Placebo", "Active"), each = 2),
  variable  = "SEX",
  .label    = rep(c("F", "M"), 2),
  .kind     = "categorical",
  stat_name = "n",
  stat      = c(12, 8, 9, 11))
p <- table_plan(st, cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(categorical = "{n}") |>
  plan_stub(name = "Characteristic")

# Minimal: the stub's heading, then each arm's name (the row is short:
# "{col}" repeats over the value columns)
pages <- p |>
  plan_col_header(rtf_col_header(c("Characteristic", "{col}"))) |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]
#> ───────────────────────────────
#> Characteristic  Placebo  Active
#> ───────────────────────────────
#> SEX                            
#>     F             12       9   
#>     M              8       11  
#> 
#> <rtftable> 3 rows x 3 columns
#>   Columns:    Characteristic | Placebo | Active
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     auto / inherited
#> 

# Each arm with its N (given here; an ARD from cards states them), and
# a spanner over both that totals them
pages <- p |>
  plan_col_header(
    values = list(n = c(Placebo = 20, Active = 20)),
    lines  = list(c(Characteristic = "", .values = "Treatment (N={n:sum})"),
                  c(Characteristic = "", .values = "{col}"),
                  c(Characteristic = "Characteristic", .values = "(N={n})")),
    span   = list("one", "each", "each")) |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]
#> ────────────────────────────────
#>                 Treatment (N=40)
#>                 Placebo   Active
#> Characteristic   (N=20)   (N=20)
#> ────────────────────────────────
#> SEX                             
#>     F              12       9   
#>     M              8        11  
#> 
#> <rtftable> 3 rows x 3 columns
#>   Columns:    Characteristic | Placebo | Active
#>   Header rows: 3 (spanning)
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     auto / inherited
#>
